title: Mitochondrial proteome of Acanthamoeba delineates aerobic and anaerobic pathways dynamically regulated by oxygen.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the MitoCarta Tree of Life (MitoTOL) xlsx tables from mitocarta.org for Acanthamoeba (11.5 MB), Arabidopsis (21.5 MB), Giardia, Leishmania and Trypanosoma (Babesia link returned 404). Acanthamoeba 'AllGenes' tab: 15,944 genes x 102 columns, 0 duplicate GeneIDs, AcMitoCarta 0/1 column with 1,122 positives (matches paper), 9,561 genes detected by mass spectrometry (1,115 positives among them), every column documented in a Descriptions tab. Other species: Arabidopsis 1,609/27,559, Leishmania 1,594/8,470, Trypanosoma 1,666/9,678, Giardia 59/4,968. I computed the DeepLoc2.1 mitochondrion-score baseline already in the tables: Acanthamoeba AUROC (area under the ROC curve) 0.956, average precision 0.81; Arabidopsis AP 0.76; Leishmania 0.85; Trypanosoma 0.87. No protein-sequence column in any table. GEO GSE338845 metadata: 48 RNA-seq samples.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the ACANB re-annotated protein FASTA is in MassIVE MSV000101796 (FTP listing failed, not verified); PCP (protein correlation profiling) method details and 0.6 threshold giving ~8% estimated false discovery rate; the Europe PMC supplement listing timed out, so Cell's own supplement files were not opened (the mitocarta.org file states it is Table S2).

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: direct xlsx downloads from mitocarta.org/Broad, no login. Paper is CC BY 4.0.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: 'AcMitoCarta' 0/1 column (and AtMitoCarta, LtMitoCarta, TbMitoCarta, GlMitoCarta in sister tables); also a continuous 'PCP score' column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Partial. Checked: no sequences in the tables. Arabidopsis (TAIR AGI IDs), Trypanosoma/Leishmania (TriTrypDB IDs) and Giardia (GenBank KAE accessions) map to public proteomes in one bulk download each; Acanthamoeba uses a new ACANB annotation whose FASTA is said to be on MassIVE (unverified), with UniProt best-bidirectional hits for 11,560 genes as fallback.

a4_units_stated.note: Checked: binary membership label needs no units; PCP score is a documented Pearson correlation; intensities documented as log10 normalized total intensity.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: 15,944 Acanthamoeba genes with 1,122 positives; ~66,600 genes and ~6,050 positives across the five species tables I opened.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~70 MB of xlsx plus ~70k protein sequences (~40 MB FASTA)
a6_fits_laptop.note: ESM-2 embeddings of ~70k proteins are feasible on CPU with the 35M/150M checkpoints; head training is seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Checked: 1,122 AcMitoCarta and 1,084 MitoViaPCP match the abstract/tab descriptions; 15,944 total = 1,122 + 14,822 quoted in text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Checked evidence column: 984 PCP-only, 74 PCP+microscopy, 26 PCP+mtDNA, 22 microscopy-only, 16 mtDNA-only. PCP is a mass-spectrometry fractionation measurement, not a sequence prediction; DeepLoc/TargetP are separate annotation columns and only enter the benchmark labels, not AcMitoCarta. Caveat: undetected proteins (6,383) are labelled 0 by default, so negatives among them are untested.

B1.why: One table per species with documented GeneID key; sequences must be joined from separate proteome FASTAs.

B2.why: xlsx parsed first try with pandas; multi-tab, header row fine. Not csv but trivial.

B3.why: Same uniform PCP workflow across MitoTOL species per paper; labels already binary 0/1 by authors.

B4.why: No censored values, but 6,383 Acanthamoeba genes undetected by MS (PCP=-1) default to negative; drop or flag.

B5.why: 0 duplicate GeneIDs checked; protein groups already collapsed to genes by authors.

B6.why: Descriptions tab documents every column, checked in file.

C1.why: Leave-one-species-out transfer tells whether localization learned on model organisms holds in divergent protists either way.

C2.why: DeepLoc2.1, TargetP2.0, MitoFates open; DeepLoc already AUROC 0.956 here (computed from file).

C3.why: Diversity angle: first uniform experimental mitoproteomes across five distant eukaryotes; but strong baseline limits headroom.

C4.why: Each mitoproteome required purification, DIA mass spectrometry, transfection lines and microscopy.

C5.why: DeepLoc2.1 and TargetP scores already columns; per-species APs 0.76–0.87 computed directly.

D1.why: ESM-2 open weights, protein sequences are the natural input.

D2.why: Mean-pooled plus N-terminal ESM-2 embeddings cached once on CPU; logistic or MLP head.

D3.why: ESM-2 MIT licence; paper CC BY 4.0; data public on mitocarta.org.

E1.why: Leave-one-species-out split plus orthogroup-cluster holdout; orthogroups (OG_ID) present in Leishmania table.

E2.why: Five species tables opened, plus human MitoCarta3.0 and yeast lists as extra groups.

E3.why: Prevalence baseline (1.2%–19% per species) and DeepLoc score baseline both computable.

E4.why: Three biological replicates per fraction in the table; PCP score per replicate subset estimable; ~8% FDR stated.

E5.why: mtDNA-encoded proteins and orthologs of human MitoCarta3.0 (goldp: 261/296 positive) must score highest.

E6.why: Label shuffle and N-terminus-only versus mature-sequence ablations are straightforward.

E7.why: Hold out whole species; Gawryluk 2014 Acanthamoeba mitoproteome and human MitoCarta3.0 are independent sets.

E8.why: DeepLoc AUROC/AP reproducible from columns in file; paper's own TargetP 46% (514/1,122) recovered as 45.8%.

G1.why: Species-specific gene IDs (TAIR, TriTrypDB, GenBank, ACANB) plus UniProt best hits; resolution needed for Acanthamoeba.

G2.why: Human MitoCarta3.0, yeast mitoproteome, UniProt subcellular-location annotations, joinable on UniProt.

G3.why: Gene-to-protein is one-to-one after best-transcript choice; ACANB-to-UniProt via BLAST hits is many-to-one at times.

G4.why: Combined: do opisthokont-trained localization rules transfer to amoebozoa, plants, kinetoplastids and Giardia?

H1.why: Detected non-mitochondrial proteins with low PCP scores are real negatives (8,446 in Acanthamoeba).

H2.why: Five distant species, but one consortium, one protocol, one strain each.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, restricted to MS-detected proteins in lab-cultured strains.

H4.why: Paper discusses detection-limited low-abundance proteins; undetected-as-negative default is only in the column notes.

I1.why: MitoTOL consortium (Mootha, Calvo labs) and parasite drug-target groups; DeepLoc developers at DTU.

I2.why: Better predictor would prioritise which unexplored protist proteins to tag; marginal given DeepLoc already strong.

I3.why: Average precision at low prevalence matches the decision: which candidates to tag and image.

I4.why: DeepLoc plus TargetP threshold already gives AP 0.76–0.87; ML gain likely in the residual cases.

J1.why: Embedding caching, grouped cross-species splits, calibration and transfer evaluation.

J2.why: Mitochondrial biology is interpretable via known complexes, but protist specifics need checking.

J3.why: DeepLoc cross-species benchmark on the new experimental sets is shareable even before any new model.

J4.why: Roughly two to three weeks plausible; not formally set.

existing_models.name: DeepLoc 2.1 (protein-language-model subcellular localization predictor, DTU)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not evaluated by its authors on these sets; I computed from the file AUROC 0.956 / average precision 0.81 on Acanthamoeba, AP 0.76 Arabidopsis, 0.85 Leishmania, 0.87 Trypanosoma, on proteins likely absent from its training data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved from DeepLoc paper; search results note localization predictors underperform on multilocalizing proteins and fine compartments.

existing_models.name: TargetP 2.0 (N-terminal targeting signal predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: Paper: only 46% (514/1,122) of AcMitoCarta proteins have a predicted mitochondrial targeting sequence vs 1% of others; confirmed 45.8% vs 0.8% from file.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: This paper: targeting-signal predictors miss over half of the experimental mitoproteome, hence need for experiment.

integration.partner_dataset: Human MitoCarta3.0 and yeast mitoproteome plus the four other MitoTOL species tables
integration.join_key: Species gene ID to proteome FASTA; UniProt accession for cross-resource
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the sequence rules for mitochondrial import learned from animals, fungi and plants hold across deeply divergent eukaryotes, and which lineage-specific proteins break them?

controls.positive_control: mtDNA-encoded proteins and orthologs of human MitoCarta3.0 genes (261/296 gold+ are positive) must rank top; recover the TargetP mTP enrichment (45.8% vs 0.8%).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within species; random-embedding features; check undetected-protein negatives do not drive the score.
controls.external_validation: Leave-one-species-out across five MitoTOL tables; Gawryluk 2014 Acanthamoeba list; human MitoCarta3.0.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts whether a protein detected by mass spectrometry in a lab-grown strain co-fractionates with mitochondria, transferring across five MitoTOL eukaryotes, compared against DeepLoc2.1, which already reaches 0.76–0.87 average precision.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's amino-acid sequence to predict whether it lives in mitochondria, testing on distant single-celled organisms not used for training.
plain_idea.train_on: Protein sequences from four of five species with experimentally measured mitochondrial membership (about 66,600 genes, about 6,050 mitochondrial, verified in the tables), plus human and yeast lists.
plain_idea.predict: Yes/no mitochondrial for each protein of the held-out species; truth comes from mass-spectrometry co-fractionation with mitochondrial markers, mitochondrial-DNA encoding, or tagged-protein microscopy.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Parasite and protist labs could prioritise drug targets and tagging experiments in species without a measured mitoproteome; a failure tells us where current predictors' rules break.

more_or_better_data.why: Five uniformly measured mitoproteomes from amoebozoa, plant, kinetoplastids and Giardia (~6,050 positives) cover lineages poorly represented in UniProt-derived training sets; total size is not larger than DeepLoc's training set.

confidence_score.why: Continuous PCP scores and triplicate fractions let us model label noise and calibrate; DeepLoc gives scores but not calibrated per-lineage uncertainty (not verified in its paper).

models_beatable.why: DeepLoc 2.1 (protein language model, 2022/2024) already scores AP 0.76–0.87 on these held-out species; TargetP 2.0 (2019) is clearly weaker at 46% recall.

guaranteed_improvement.why: DeepLoc can be run as baseline and a model could use its score plus MitoTOL data, but labels here (co-fractionation) differ from DeepLoc's literature annotations, so improvement is not guaranteed.

label_elsewhere.sources: Human MitoCarta3.0 (~1,136 genes, known resource), yeast Morgenstern mitoproteome (900 genes, cited in paper), UniProt subcellular location annotations (known resource), Human Protein Atlas localization (known resource), four other MitoTOL tables (opened).
label_elsewhere.why: Extra labelled species allow genuine leave-one-lineage-out tests rather than random splits within one organism.

ambitious.why: Publishes biology-first ML; would need a model clearly beating DeepLoc on held-out lineages and new validated protist mitochondrial proteins.

realistic.why: Publishes benchmarks of predictors; a cross-lineage benchmark of DeepLoc/TargetP versus an ESM-2 head on MitoTOL data fits.

fallback.why: Accepts benchmark notes and negative results, e.g. that DeepLoc already transfers and new heads add little.

pitch.headline: Five uniformly measured experimental mitoproteomes across deeply divergent eukaryotes, about 6,050 positives in about 66,600 genes, publicly downloadable as documented tables.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Same mass-spectrometry co-fractionation protocol for an amoeba, a plant, two trypanosomatids and Giardia; Acanthamoeba alone has 15,944 genes, 1,122 positives, 0 duplicates, all columns documented.
pitch.the_win: A leave-one-species-out model beating DeepLoc 2.1's average precision of 0.81 on Acanthamoeba and 0.76 on Arabidopsis.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A first honest cross-lineage benchmark of open localization predictors on experimental protist mitoproteomes, showing which lineage-specific proteins (e.g. 381 lacking human/yeast homologs) they miss.
pitch.who_wants_it: MitoTOL consortium (Mootha and Calvo labs, Broad) choosing which species and proteins to tag next; DeepLoc developers; parasite drug-target groups.

ml_idea: Embed all proteins from the five MitoTOL species with frozen ESM-2 (whole-sequence plus N-terminal window), train a logistic/MLP head leave-one-species-out on MS-detected proteins, and compare against DeepLoc2.1 and TargetP scores already in the tables; report average precision per held-out species and on proteins without human/yeast homologs.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: ~70k sequences at ~3–4 per second with ESM-2 150M on CPU; baseline AUCs were timed in seconds from the xlsx.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Obtain the ACANB protein FASTA from MassIVE MSV000101796 (or confirm UniProt best hits cover most of the 1,122 positives) and confirm TriTrypDB/TAIR/GenBank IDs map to sequences for >95% of rows.

verdict_reason: Clean, documented multi-species labels verified in files, but DeepLoc already reaches AUROC 0.956 here and Acanthamoeba sequences must still be retrieved; confirm sequence access first, and expect a benchmark rather than a big win.
